subject: Roadmap & commit request — CloudLayer MAP draft and pricing
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Goodman <rachel@cloudlayer.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@cloudlayer.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Roadmap & commit request — CloudLayer MAP draft and pricing

Hi Rachel / Samir,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great discussion and I appreciate the clarity on your Q1 usage profile. Attached is the first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) we promised (CloudLayer_MAP_v1.2.xlsx). Key points summarized below so we have alignment before I loop in pricing:

- Target close: 2027-01-14 (you mentioned end of Q1 procurement window as a soft deadline)
- Initial commit ask: 60k inference hours (3-month ramp to steady-state) with committed discount tiers applied
- Milestone ownership: CloudLayer PM (Rachel) signoff on integration tests by 2027-01-04; Redwood to deliver private VPC template and SOC2 evidence by 2026-12-20
- Dependencies: procurement PO, legal SOW signoff, and confirmation of required regions (us-west + us-east)

Next steps I propose: you review the MAP and mark any changes to milestones/owners, then I’ll escalate the commit/credit ask to our pricing team for approval and return a finalized SOW. If you’re comfortable, please confirm the target close date and whether the 60k commit is a reasonable starting point, or if you need a lower starter commitment + ramp.

Attachments: CloudLayer_MAP_v1.2.xlsx, SOW-draft-CloudLayer.docx

Thanks,
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
viv@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

---
From: Rachel Goodman <rachel@cloudlayer.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@cloudlayer.com>, Procurement <procurement@cloudlayer.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Roadmap & commit request — CloudLayer MAP draft and pricing

Vivek,

Appreciate the clear summary and the MAP draft. Quick answers after a quick review with the team:

- Target close: 2027-01-21 (one week later than your proposed date to allow for procurement windows at the end of the month)
- Commit: we can do a pilot commitment of 30k inference hours with a 30-60-90 ramp to 60k if performance and costs line up
- Milestones: we’ll own integration test signoff; we'll need Redwood to confirm KMS/HSM requirements and whether the VPC template can support our existing transit gateway
- Pricing ask: procurement asked whether you can include a one-time migration credit or onboarding credit (they suggested $30k credit) and a 12% discount on committed pricing for the first year

I’ve attached a redline on the MAP (inline comments in the spreadsheet). Procurement will be the main approver on the PO and credits.

-Rachel
Rachel Goodman
Head of Platform, CloudLayer

---
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 13:20:00 -0800
Subject: FWD: Roadmap & commit request — CloudLayer MAP draft and pricing (pricing/credit ask)

Ben / Aditya,

Looping you both in — CloudLayer (related account DL-4791) responded with a revised target close and a pricing/credit request:

Summary:
- Industry: fintech-like workloads (low- to mid- latency, high token volumes)
- They propose a pilot commit of 30k inference hours, ramping to 60k; target close 2027-01-21
- They are requesting a $30k onboarding/migration credit + ~12% committed discount for year one
- Dependencies: confirmation re KMS/HSM and VPC transit gateway support (legal/procurement will hold PO until those are satisfied)

Ask: can we approve a one-time $30k credit + up to 12% discount contingent on a signed 12-month reserved commit at 60k hours? If not, what is the counter we should present (e.g., smaller credit + higher commit requirement or staged credits tied to milestone acceptance)?

Recommended approach (my suggestion):
- Approve a $20k onboarding credit upfront + an additional $10k credit released on integration-test signoff (ties credit to milestone)
- Approve up to 10% first-year committed discount if they sign 12-month reserved capacity at 60k; if they start with a 30k pilot we should require a shorter lock or higher effective pricing until they convert

I’ve attached the MAP and SOW redline from their team. Need an approval or counter to share with Rachel by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Vivek

---
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FWD: Roadmap & commit request — CloudLayer MAP draft and pricing (pricing/credit ask)

Vivek — thanks for the write-up. Thinking aloud:

- $20k/$10k split credit tied to milestones is reasonable and reduces risk — +1 on that approach
- 10% committed discount for 12-month at 60k seems on the edge but acceptable for a strategic customer in fintech. If legal needs to escalate, we can frame it as ‘up to 10% subject to finance sign-off and PO timing’
- For a 30k pilot we should offer a transitional SKU with a 6-month term and a 5% discount, with an automatic conversion clause to the 12-month pricing if they commit up to 60k within 90 days

Approve the $20k/$10k milestone credit + up to 10% discount contingent on the 12-month commit. I’ll backstop if finance pushes back — looping Aditya for visibility on budget/finance gating.

-Ben
VP, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

---
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 08:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FWD: Roadmap & commit request — CloudLayer MAP draft and pricing (pricing/credit ask)

Agree with Ben’s approach. A couple notes from finance/legal perspective:

- Confirming the $20k upfront + $10k on integration signoff is workable, but finance requires the credit to be spelled out in the SOW with milestone acceptance criteria and payment schedule tied to the PO (we can’t issue credits without contract language)
- The 10% discount is OK if the PO is received within 30 days of SOW execution and the 12-month reserved commit is explicit in the contract; otherwise we should reduce to 7%
- Need to validate KMS/HSM compatibility; if the customer requires an HSM integration that requires engineering change we may need to add a one-time engineering services fee (TBD)

I’ll work with legal to draft the exact SOW language and the credit schedule. Vivek — please let Rachel know we have provisional approval pending PO timing + final SOW language.

-Aditya
Director, Finance (sales ops)
